title: Salma M. Thalji
text:
Vision
Drawing on my training in electrical engineering, neuroinformatics and circadian neuroscience, my vision is to help create a world where people can clearly understand how their everyday environments influence their wellbeing. I want wearable sensing, computational methods and AI to transform continuously monitored physiological signals, behavioral habits and environmental exposures into insights that feel personal, practical, and empowering. I’m committed to being a leader in the health exposome movement and designing inclusive tools that honor gender, cultural and environmental diversity.

Research Software Engineer – Technical University of Munich


February 2025 – present



Munich & Tübingen, Germany

Project: GLEE (Global Light Exposure and Experience)
An international open-science initiative developing interoperable infrastructure for wearable light exposure and optical radiation research

Lead the development of the Global Light Commons, an open-source ecosystem for standardized metadata, validation, discovery, and analysis of wearable light exposure datasets
Collaborate with international researchers to develop community standards supporting interoperable light exposure and exposome research
Develop software infrastructure for large-scale validation and characterization of wearable light exposure datasets



PhD Researcher – Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics


January 2024 – present


Research focus: Wearable light exposure, physiological signal processing, and circadian neuroscience

Characterize temporal patterns of real-world wearable light exposure to identify person-specific exposure profiles and examine their relationships with sleep-wake behavior and circadian timing
Developed dlmoR, an open-source R package for reproducible estimation of dim light melatonin onset (DLMO), published in the Journal of Biological Rhythms
Co-led physiological data collection during a forced desynchrony protocol and analyzed multimodal physiological datasets: continuous glucose monitoring, temperature, electrocardiography, blood pressure

Designed Unity-based visuomotor adaptation and tactile psychophysics experiments
